pg006_n0004: The English Pupil’s Book Standard Four has been prepared in accordance with the 2023 English Language Syllabus for Primary Education, Standards III–VI, issued by the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology.
pg006_n0005: This textbook is the Third Edition, improved from the Second Edition of 2021 of the English Pupil’s Book Standard Four, published by TIE in accordance with the 2016 Basic Education Syllabus for Standard IV.
pg006_n0007: This textbook consists of eleven units that focus on skills such as Developing vocabulary, Expressing quantity, Expressing location, Expressing past events, Expressing result and reason, Taking part in conversations and Reading for comprehension.
pg006_n0008: Others include The basic features of spoken English, Writing wishes and short messages, My daily routines and Creative writing.
pg006_n0009: The book contains learning activities and real-life examples that will enable you to express yourself appropriately and fluently in oral, signed and written English.
pg006_n0010: In addition, the book will help you expand your vocabulary that you will use in your everyday communication.
pg006_n0012: Additional learning resources are available in the TIE e-Library at https://ol.tie.go.tz or ol.tie.go.tz

pg060_n0007: When we read, we either want to obtain general or specific information.
pg060_n0008: In this unit, you will learn to read to get a message from the text.
pg060_n0009: The goal will be to get the skills of reading for general and specific information.
pg060_n0010: The competencies developed will enable you to read and get the correct message from the text.

pg060_n0015: (a) Read the following conversations between the teacher and the pupils in the classroom.
pg060_n0019: Teacher: Today, we are going to learn about something very important when reading.
pg060_n0020: Does anyone know what “reading for general information” means?
pg060_n0022: Pupil 1: Is it when you read a book?
pg060_n0025: Yes, it involves reading, but it’s a special type of reading.
pg060_n0026: When we read for general information, we read to get a basic understanding of a topic.
pg060_n0027: It’s like reading to know a little about something, not everything.
pg061_n0002: Pupil 2: Oh! Like when we read a story just to enjoy it?
pg061_n0003: Teacher: Exactly! But reading for general information isn’t just for stories.
pg061_n0004: You can read newspapers, textbooks, or even posters on the walls.
pg061_n0005: The goal is to understand the main ideas, not every small detail.
pg061_n0006: Pupil 3: So, we don’t have to remember everything we read?
pg061_n0008: You just need to understand the general idea.
pg061_n0009: For example, if you’re reading a book about animals, you don’t need to know how every animal lives, but you should understand that animals live in different places and eat different things.
pg061_n0010: Pupil 4: Can we ask questions if we don’t understand?
pg061_n0012: Asking questions helps you understand the general information better.
pg061_n0013: And after reading, you can tell someone what the main points were.

pg061_n0016: You can read many things for general information, like your school textbooks, signs in the community, newspapers, or even a magazine.

pg061_n0020: I’ll give you a short paragraph to read.
pg061_n0021: Your task is to tell me the main idea when you finish.

pg077_n0018: Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Pendo who loved making her friends and family feel special.
pg077_n0019: She has always wanted to learn how to write best wishes for different occasions.
pg077_n0020: One day, her teacher, Mr Mussa, decided to teach the class about writing heartfelt wishes.
pg077_n0022: Mr Mussa began, “Wishes are special words that make people feel happy, loved, and cared for.
pg077_n0023: Today, we will learn how to write three types of wishes: Birthday Wishes, Best Wishes for Exams, and Get Well Soon Wishes.”
pg078_n0002: Pendo listened carefully as Mr Mussa explained the first type of wish: Birthday Wishes.
pg078_n0003: “When someone is celebrating their birthday,” Mr Mussa said, “it’s a special day for them.
pg078_n0004: We can wish them a ‘Happy Birthday’ to make them feel joyful and loved.”
pg078_n0005: He wrote an example on the board:
pg078_n0006: “Happy Birthday! May your day be filled with fun, laughter, and lots of cake!”
pg078_n0008: “And to make it even more special, you can mention something they love.
pg078_n0009: For example: ‘Happy Birthday! I hope you get to play your favourite game today!’”
pg078_n0011: Pendo smiled, imagining writing a birthday wish for her best friend, Samwel, who loved playing basketball.
pg078_n0013: Next, Mr Mussa talked about Best Wishes for Exams.
pg078_n0014: “When our friends or classmates have exams, we can send them good wishes to encourage them to do their best,” he explained.
pg078_n0016: “Good luck on your exam! I know you have worked hard, and you will do great!”
pg078_n0018: “You could also say, ‘Do your best and believe in yourself.
pg078_n0021: Pendo thought about her friend Maria, who often felt nervous before exams.
pg078_n0022: She decided to write a supportive wish for her to help boost her confidence.
pg078_n0024: Finally, Mr Mussa discussed Get Well Soon Wishes.
pg078_n0025: “If someone we know is not feeling well, we can send them a wish to help them feel better,” he said.
pg078_n0027: “Get well soon! We miss you and hope you feel better quickly.”
pg078_n0029: “You could also add something comforting, like, ‘Sending you lots of love and hugs.
pg078_n0030: I hope you feel stronger and healthier every day!’”
pg078_n0032: Pendo nodded, thinking of her cousin who had been feeling sick.
pg078_n0033: She knew just what to write to cheer her up.
pg079_n0002: Mr Mussa wrapped up the lesson by saying, “When writing a wish, always think about how you want the other person to feel.
pg079_n0003: Be kind, use encouraging words, and try to make them smile.
pg079_n0004: Add something special that shows you care about them.
pg079_n0005: Remember, your words can make a big difference!”
pg079_n0007: After the lesson, Pendo felt excited.
pg079_n0008: She could not wait to write her wishes to brighten someone’s day.
pg079_n0009: She knew now that her words could bring joy, comfort, and encouragement to the people she cared about with a little thought and kindness.

pg013_n0044_easy_read: Every Saturday, Tupendane Market is full of people.
pg013_n0045_easy_read: Buyers and sellers gathered with their voices buzzing all around the market place.
pg013_n0046_easy_read: The smell of fresh fruits and vegetables filled the air, making it the perfect place to shop for the week.
pg014_n0002_easy_read: Mwanaidi, a friendly fruit seller, carefully arranged her guava and watermelon on her stall.
pg014_n0003_easy_read: Each fruit had a price tag attached, with the guavas going for 100 shillings each, and the watermelons for 2000 shillings.
pg014_n0005_easy_read: Next to her, Rejo, another seller, was busy displaying his tomatoes and onions in neat piles.
pg014_n0006_easy_read: Rejo smiled when he saw Mwanaidi.
pg014_n0009_easy_read: Rejo asked as he wiped sweat from his brow.
pg014_n0011_easy_read: "Morning, Rejo! Business is going well, but I wish more buyers would come early."
pg014_n0014_easy_read: Just then, a mother and her little boy came to Mwanaidi's stall.
pg014_n0015_easy_read: The boy looked very happy and pointed at a ripe watermelon.
pg014_n0016_easy_read: "Mum, can we buy 1 of those big watermelons?"
pg014_n0022_easy_read:
"It is 2000 shillings, but you are my first buyer today.
I will give you a discount.
pg014_n0023_easy_read: You can have it for 1500 shillings."
pg014_n0024_easy_read: Mwanaidi said with a big smile.
pg014_n0027_easy_read: The mother replied and gave her the money.
pg014_n0029_easy_read:
The woman left with what she bought.
Then Mwanaidi turned to Rejo.
pg014_n0030_easy_read: "See, the key to selling is knowing when to offer a small discount!"
pg014_n0032_easy_read: Meanwhile, on the other side of the market, Yobu was selling colourful clothes and utensils.
pg014_n0033_easy_read: Yobu watched a woman as she looked at a bright fabric and some utensils.
pg014_n0039_easy_read: Yobu said, pointing to the price tag.
pg015_n0002_easy_read: "Could you give me a lower price?" she asked, with a shy smile.
pg015_n0005_easy_read: "For you, I can lower the price to 35,000 shillings, but not less.
pg015_n0006_easy_read: The price of getting these rice cookers from the factory has gone up!"
pg015_n0008_easy_read: "Alright!" the woman said, and gave him the money.
pg015_n0010_easy_read: Back at Mwanaidi's stall, Rejo started selling his grains. He talked with customers about the freshest produce in the market.
